subject: Social Media
title: The Personalization Paradox
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Personalization Paradox usable.

hook.text: Two people search the same word on Google. They get different results. Neither knows the other's version.

buildup.text: Google personalizes by location, history, device, and clicks. Truly neutral search died years ago.

discovery.text: DuckDuckGo was built on this insight: one search should give one set of results for everyone.

twist.text: Studies found Google's personalization is actually modest—about 12% variation between users.

climax.text: The real bubble isn't in search. It's in social feeds, where personalization runs far deeper.

quiz.question: How much does Google personalization typically vary between users?
